imd.title: IMD extended range forecast (weekly press release), 12 November 2026: current weather status and extended range forecast for the next two weeks (12 to 25 November 2026)
imd.summary: IMD expects a low pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal around 13 November to intensify into a depression around 15 November and, by model consensus, into a cyclonic storm over the central Bay of Bengal. It gives no rainfall category for South Peninsular India in either week; for 19–25 November it expects isolated heavy rain over Tamil Nadu and Kerala on some days, with rainfall distribution depending on the cyclonic storm's track and landfall. Rainfall for the country as a whole is likely to be below normal in both weeks.

weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.text: A low pressure area is likely over the southeast Bay of Bengal on 13 November, intensifying into a depression over the central parts of the south Bay of Bengal around 15 November and further thereafter. IMD gives no specific rainfall statement or category for South Peninsular India this week; rainfall for the country as a whole is likely to be below normal.

regional_text.Rayalaseema: Not named in the release; IMD gives no rainfall statement or category for South Peninsular India this week.
regional_text.Tamil Nadu: Not named for this week; IMD gives no rainfall statement or category for South Peninsular India, while a depression is forecast to develop over the south Bay of Bengal around 15 November.

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.text: Isolated heavy rainfall is likely over Tamil Nadu and Kerala on some days. The rainfall distribution will depend on the track and landfall area of the impending cyclonic storm; rainfall for the country as a whole is likely to be below normal.

regional_text.Rayalaseema: Not named in the release; rainfall distribution will depend on the track and landfall area of the impending cyclonic storm.
regional_text.Tamil Nadu: Isolated heavy rainfall likely on some days; rainfall distribution will depend on the track and landfall area of the impending cyclonic storm.

season.text: IMD's monthly outlook for November 2026: rainfall over South Peninsular India (Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam, Rayalaseema, Kerala & Mahe and South Interior Karnataka taken together) is most likely to be below normal (less than 77% of the long-period average of about 118.7 mm).
